key_insight: DFT predicts stronger vacancy association in CrN than TiN, with compact mixed-vacancy clusters remaining stabilised at CrN surfaces but becoming unfavourable at TiN surfaces.
engineering_relevance: Material choice, nitrogen chemical potential, and proximity to surfaces can influence vacancy populations and clustering in TiN and CrN coatings.
method: DFT comparison of native vacancies in rocksalt TiN and CrN bulk and (001) surfaces.
Formation energies evaluated within phase-stability-constrained chemical potential ranges.
Association energies referenced to isolated vacancies, using preferred depths for surface comparisons.
evidence_signal: Compact two-metal/two-nitrogen vacancy clusters have bulk-to-surface association energies of +0.217 to −0.346 eV per vacancy in TiN and +1.188 to +0.431 eV per vacancy in CrN, where positive values favour association.
watch_item: The abstract reports energetic preferences, not experimental validation or vacancy migration kinetics, so clustering rates in operating coatings remain uncertain.
paper_title: Native vacancy energetics and association in TiN and CrN: chemical potential dependence, clustering, and surface effects
